name: Array
summary: Contiguous fixed-layout memory. Fast random access, expensive to resize or shift.

name: Linked List
summary: Nodes with pointers to the next (and prev, if doubly). No resizing cost, no random access.

name: Stack
summary: LIFO. Push/pop from the same end. Backing store is usually an array or linked list.

name: Queue
summary: FIFO. Use collections.deque in Python — a list is O(n) to pop from the front.

name: Hash Map / Set
summary: Key → bucket via hash function. Average O(1) ops; degrades to O(n) on heavy collisions.

name: Binary Tree
summary: Each node has at most 2 children. No ordering guarantee — that's what makes it a BST instead.

name: Binary Search Tree
summary: Left < node < right at every subtree. In-order traversal yields sorted order.

name: Heap / Priority Queue
summary: Complete binary tree stored in an array. Min-heap or max-heap — root is always the extreme.

name: Trie
summary: Tree of characters. Each node = map of children + end-of-word flag. Great for prefix queries.

name: Graph (Adjacency List)
summary: Map of node -> list of neighbors. Space-efficient for sparse graphs (E << V^2).

name: Union-Find (Disjoint Set)
summary: Tracks connectivity between elements. Path compression + union by rank make it nearly O(1).

name: Binary Search
summary: Halve the search space each step. Requires sorted data or a monotonic feasibility check.

name: BFS
summary: Level-by-level traversal using a queue. Finds shortest path in an unweighted graph.

name: DFS
summary: Explore as deep as possible before backtracking. Recursive or iterative with an explicit stack.

name: Two-Pointer Skeleton
summary: Two indices moving toward/away from each other over sorted or linear data.

name: Backtracking Skeleton
summary: Choose, explore, un-choose. Prune early whenever the partial state can't lead to a valid answer.

name: Dynamic Programming (1D bottom-up)
summary: Build up from base cases using a recurrence. Define dp[i] in words before writing the transition.

complexity.space: O(n), or O(1) with rolling variables

name: Merge Sort
summary: Divide, sort halves, merge. Stable and predictable — good when worst-case guarantees matter.

name: Quick Sort
summary: Partition around a pivot, recurse on both sides. Fast in practice, worst case on bad pivots.

name: Dijkstra's Algorithm
summary: Shortest path in a weighted graph with non-negative edges, using a min-heap of (distance, node).
